Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroDef Technologies Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroDef Technologies' Q3 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Strategy Officer; and David Patel, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning. AeroDef Technologies delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense, and services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, we'll highlight our strong aftermarket and services revenue growth, updated full-year guidance, key drivers behind aftermarket performance, robust free cash flow generation, expansion in service offerings and customer base, improving commercial aircraft delivery rates, and revenue performance by segment.

We're particularly excited about the recent advancements in our F-35 Lightning II sustainment program and its potential to solidify our leadership in global defense sustainment for years to come. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily as fleet utilization climbs.

John Harlan:
Thank you, Michael. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $10.2 billion, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted earnings per share were $3.45. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $5.2 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year has been updated upward, as I'll detail shortly. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Our specific financial highlights include gross margin expansion to 28.5%, operating income of $2.1 billion, and free cash flow of $1.1 billion for the quarter.

Let me start by breaking down revenue by segment, where we saw balanced strength across the board. Commercial aerospace delivered $4.1 billion, up 28% year-over-year, fueled by accelerating OEM production ramps and air traffic surpassing 105% of 2019 peaks according to IATA. This segment now represents 40% of total revenue, with deliveries of AeroJet 500 narrowbody shipsets hitting 180 units, up 35%, and widebody Horizon 800 contributions at $850 million, rising 22%. North America drove 55% of the growth, Europe 25%, and Asia-Pacific surged 45% from carriers like IndiGo and Air India expanding fleets. Our backlog here grew 18% to $65 billion at a 1.4x book-to-bill, positioning us for 20-25% growth into 2025, supported by sustainability initiatives like our SFM-50 blended-wing body targeting 20% fuel burn reductions.

Defense came in at $4.5 billion, up 9% year-over-year and 44% of revenue, anchored by steady U.S. DoD funding from the FY24 NDAA's $886 billion topline. Hypersonics via the Titan IV program ramped to $1.2 billion, plus 15%, with LRIP Lot 3 deliveries amid China-Taiwan tensions. F-35 aft fuselage sustainment added $1.1 billion, up 12%, alongside UH-90 rotary-wing upgrades at $900 million and missiles/ISR at $1.3 billion. U.S. DoD was 70%, EMEA up 18% on F-35 exports and GCAP tech transfers, with $105 billion backlog at 1.2x book-to-bill. We guide 8-12% growth for the year, with upside from budget plus-ups.

Services rounded out at $1.6 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 16% of revenue, driven by MRO demand as fleet utilization hits 85%. Commercial repairs were $950 million, up 18%, especially LEAP nacelle overhauls, while defense PBL contracts hit $450 million, up 8%. Digital analytics boosted parts sales 14% to $200 million. Backlog is $15 billion, and post-Redwire acquisition, we're targeting 15% CAGR in engine services.

Diving deeper into aftermarket and services, which grew 18% year-over-year to $1.2 billion this quarter—our ninth straight quarter of double-digit gains—this segment now stands at 42% of total revenue, with margins up 220 basis points to 28.5%. Commercial aftermarket, 55% of the segment at $660 million up 22%, benefited from global fleet utilization at 85% of pre-pandemic levels per IATA, pent-up travel, and narrowbody MRO for CFM56 and LEAP on 737s and A320s. Shop visits rose 15% sequentially; we processed 450 engines using our Greenville facility's additive manufacturing, cutting turnaround 25%. North America was 60% of growth via Delta and United A320neo ramps, Europe 28% on widebodies through Safran JV, and Asia-Pacific 35% from IndiGo and AirAsia, prompting a $150 million Singapore expansion.

Defense services rose 14% to $540 million, 45% of the segment, via F-35 wing-box and avionics at $220 million up 20% on Lot 15 ramps and sortie rates at Eglin AFB. NDAA funding added $2.8 billion in task orders for Patriot PAC-3 MSE. Middle East spiked 25% with Saudi and Israel THAAD extensions, Europe $80 million from Eurofighter via MTU amid Ukraine aid. Our PHM platform with GE Blade Watch cut unscheduled maintenance 30%, driving 40% higher renewals across 2,500 platforms and $300 million in digital revenue—25% of segment. Book-to-bill at 1.3x built a $15.2 billion backlog up 12%. We expect 15-17% growth FY24, defense at 18%, margins mid-28s on AI forecasting.

The drivers of this aftermarket performance are multifaceted. Fleet utilization—IFH on LEAP and AD-400 turbofans—is 18-22% above pre-pandemic, with commercial narrowbodies at 11.8 daily hours versus 10.2 last year; defense F-35/F-15EX up 28% on NATO ops and Middle East tempo, plus $2.7 billion NDAA readiness funds. Maintenance cycles accelerated with OEM delivery lags compressing C-checks to 18-24 months and LEAP TBOs 10-12% faster at 92% part utilization. North America saw 25% unscheduled removals on aging 737NGs, Europe Ryanair/easyJet bookings through Q2 2025, Asia 35% from IndiGo CFM56s, Middle East offset by F-35 spikes. AeroPredict AI digital twins cut no-fault-founds 27%, on-wing time 15%, adding $180 million digital revenue up 55%; supply chain stocking slashed lead times 40% to 98% OEE. Dynamic pricing up 8-10%, Vector acquisition added rotors, 10-year F-35 PBLs worth $3.2 billion. Q4 growth 20-23%, FY margins 28.5%.

On free cash flow, Q3 generation was strong at $1.1 billion, contributing to YTD progress toward our record pace. Full-year 2023 we hit $4.2 billion up 28%, exceeding guidance by $400 million—eighth straight positive year. Operating cash $7.8 billion up 22% from missiles hypersonics milestones, F-35 optimizations dropping DSO to 65 days. EBITDA margins 14.2% despite inflation via AI scrap reductions 18% at Camden. CapEx $3.6 billion or 4.1% of $88 billion revenue: 45% munitions capacity, 30% DEW R&D, 25% AM titanium. U.S. 65% cash gen from $145 billion backlog, international 25% Middle East/Europe, APAC 10% AUKUS, commercial 15% rebound.

Utilization: 35% or $1.5 billion to deleverage to 2.2x, $800 million pensions; 30% or $1.3 billion shareholder returns—$900 million dividends up 10% at 2.1% yield, $400 million repurchases retiring 1.2% shares; 35% or $1.4 billion growth—$600 million supply chain rare earths/alt-materials, $500 million NGAD digital twins/lasers, $300 million LEO. FY24 guide $4.5-5.0 billion, CapEx $3.8-4.0 billion, margins 14.7%.

Finally, our updated full-year 2024 guidance reflects first-half outperformance, international acceleration, supply chain easing. Revenue now $30.2-30.8 billion, 9-12% growth; adjusted EPS $13.60-14.00, 11% at midpoint. Defense $19.8-20.2 billion on NGAD/F-35 LRIP, 1.3x book-to-bill, Poland/Romania PAC-3 FMS, GPI quals; margins 11.5-12.0% on AM cost-outs 15%, Huntsville digital twins. Commercial $7.0-7.3 billion on 737/787/A320neo ramps, titanium easing 40%; margins 9.0-9.5%. Space $3.3-3.4 billion on GPS IIIF, SDA T2TL, DEW HELIOS; margins 10.5-11.0%. Operating margin 10.8-11.2%, FCF $3.2-3.5 billion, backlog $52 billion up 14%, tax 21-22%. Assumptions: mid-single inflation, USD headwind $200M, geo tailwinds AUKUS/ISR; risks shutdowns/Boeing strikes, but 85% fixed-price insulates. CapEx $1.2 billion hypersonics/AI, targeting 200bps accretion by 2026.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, John. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like the F-35 and Titan IV. We're investing in automation and digital technologies, including Siemens NX digital twins across 85% of assembly lines reducing non-conformance 22%, and additive manufacturing for titanium brackets cutting lead times from 16 to 6 weeks with 15,000 parts YTD. In commercial, Q3 deliveries hit 162 units up 28% YoY—112 737 MAX, 28 787s, 22 A320neo fuselages—at 92% utilization, first-time quality 98.5%. Recovery at 68% of 2019 quarterly peaks (612 YTD), targeting 75% year-end, 85% 2025, full by 2027 on 10-12% RPK CAGR. LEAP ramps to 1,200/month, titanium $25/kg stable; backlog 5,200 units $420 billion. North America 42%, APAC 31% growth engine, Europe 18%. Sustainability: 20% SAF composites, hydrogen APUs.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. On the technology front, we're advancing next-generation propulsion and hypersonics. Our LEAP overhauls and GEnx PHM with Blade Watch reduce events 30%; hypersonic Glide Phase Interceptor wind tunnel quals passed; 300kW laser endurance tests for HELIOS; gallium nitride antennas for SATCOM/JADC2. Digital twins, IoT on 15 petabytes telemetry improve availability 15-20%; AeroPredict cuts MTTR 30%. These give us a competitive edge.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Elena. Strategically, we're expanding service offerings and customer base. Services up 28% to $1.2 billion, 42% of revenue, RPO $28.5 billion up 18%, 1.3x book-to-bill. PBL covers 65% fixed-wing, $750 million C-130J extension with AI predictive maintenance cutting downtime 22%. DEW services +45%, Orbital Sustainment $320 million NASA COTS. International 35% revenue: Poland/Finland $1.1 billion FMS Patriot/NASAMS, Korea $900 million hypersonics. U.S. Space Force $450 million PNT, commercial MRO +32% to $180 million, 14 new Tier-1s, 185 customers 92% retention. Services 75% margins vs. 35% hardware; $4.5 billion pursuits JADC2/F-15QA. FY24 growth 25-30%.

David Patel:
Thanks, Robert. Marketing efforts underscore demand signals, with strong pipeline in Middle East and APAC.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Sarah Klein with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Klein:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the aftermarket revenue growth and its drivers?

Michael Reynolds:
Certainly, Sarah. As John detailed, aftermarket grew 18% to $1.2 billion, ninth double-digit quarter, now 42% of revenue at 28.5% margins. Commercial up 22% on 85% utilization, 450 engines processed; defense 14% on F-35 $220 million, THAAD/Eurofighter. PHM digital $300 million, backlog $15.2 billion. Drivers: IFH 18-22% above pre-COVID, maintenance compressing on aging fleets, AeroPredict AI boosting on-wing 15%. We're capturing share in $120 billion TAM.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Rivera:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about the updated full-year guidance and key assumptions?

John Harlan:
Mike, we're raising to $30.2-30.8 billion revenue, EPS $13.60-14.00. Defense on NGAD/F-35, international PAC-3; commercial ramps; space SDA/DEW. FCF $3.2-3.5 billion, backlog $52 billion. Embeds inflation easing, geo tailwinds, insulated by fixed-price.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Grant with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Grant:
Regarding the commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery trajectory?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Lisa, Q2 deliveries 162 up 28%, 68% 2019 recovery targeting 75% year-end. 737 MAX 112, 787 28; backlog 5,200 units. Supply normalizing LEAP/titanium, digital twins 98.5% quality. APAC leading growth, synergies to defense R&D.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
